title: Docker image publishing: floating latest tags move only when the release is GitHub's canonical Latest
answers: Why did a patch release move the Docker latest or latest-full image tag?
How do I change which image tags get promoted to latest after a release?
Where is the logic that decides whether mlflow or model-server latest images are updated?
How are versioned GHCR images published without touching latest?
body:
Path: .github/workflows/push-images.yml (job push-images, then check-latest and promote-latest) runs on release publish. It builds and pushes versioned ghcr.io/mlflow/mlflow, mlflow-full and model-server tags via docker/metadata-action with flavor latest=false, and then copies them to latest, latest-full and model-server:latest.
Rule: The build job must never emit floating tags. Floating tags are written only by promote-latest, using `docker buildx imagetools create` from the versioned tag. It runs only when check-latest finds that `gh api repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/releases/latest` returns github.event.release.tag_name. promote-latest re-checks that same value immediately before its writes.
Symptom: A maintenance patch release published with `gh release create --latest=false` moved the Docker latest and latest-full tags to a non-canonical version.
Constraints: Applies to release-triggered runs. A release that is not GitHub's Latest skips promotion by design and writes a step-summary note. A read failure of the Latest pointer fails closed (promote=false and the job fails) rather than promoting. This replaced the old semver comparison over `gh release list`.
applies: Any change to Docker/GHCR image tagging, latest-tag promotion, or the push-images release workflow.
says: A maintenance patch release incorrectly updated our public latest container image tags.
Why did publishing an older maintenance version overwrite the latest container image tag?
Prevent non-canonical patch releases from updating floating latest tags in the container registry.
How can we publish a versioned container image without promoting it to latest?
Only official primary releases should advance the floating latest container image pointers.
search: `.github/workflows/push-images.yml` pushes versioned container images with `latest=false` and restricts floating tag promotion (`latest`, `latest-full`, `model-server:latest`) to the `promote-latest` job using `docker buildx imagetools create`. Promotion runs only when `check-latest` confirms that the GitHub release matches the canonical release returned by `gh api repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/releases/latest`, re-checking before writing. Non-canonical releases skip promotion by design, while read failures of the latest release pointer fail closed by setting `promote=false` and failing the job. Guidance applies to release-triggered workflows for GHCR image tagging, replacing earlier semver comparisons over `gh release list`.
